GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: Delegation is a division of labor, not a planning format or a demand for maximal ceremony. The existing bounded-recovery foundation should be reused while native document loading becomes one input path into common execution. A controller can receive requirements from a native package, another document, or the current conversation. It should be able to assign meaningful reviews and act within advance user authority without losing deterministic counters or truthful acceptance.

Alternatives.Alternative: Change only prompt wording. This helps routing and avoids unnecessary questions, but cannot remove the required planPath and native source fields from checkpoint registration or let a pre-stop authorization pass through a deliberately post-stop recovery contract. It does not meet the full requested behavior.
Make external and conversation-scoped work untracked. Rejected: it would lose enforcement of assigned review obligations and bounded recovery precisely where no structured source document exists.

Add an adapter and prompt exception for every planning tool. Rejected: it creates an unbounded compatibility catalog. The controller already interprets provided requirements; runtime needs a small format-independent execution contract.

Convert every source into a new native package. Rejected: it forces unwanted files and introduces a second normative source and lifecycle. Native loading should remain an optional integration benefit.
Require a final spec/code pair for every execution. Rejected: reviewers are selected by the source, user, or controller. Runtime enforces what was assigned, not a hidden universal pair.

Remove retry limits when autonomous work is requested. Rejected: authority to work without intermediate questions is not an unlimited compute budget. A shared finite reserve supports advance authorization without endless renewal.

Allow any earlier message through the existing post-stop authorization validator. Rejected: that would weaken replay and scope boundaries. Advance execution authority is a distinct validated record with finite consumption.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: The implementation plan chooses the smallest additive tool shape for generic execution and dynamic checkpoints. Reuse work_item_open, work_item_decide, review-only work items, and work_checkpoint where their contracts remain clear; do not add a parallel tool family merely to avoid refactoring source assumptions.

Common workflow types currently depend on native extraction types. The plan should establish a shared execution contract with the native adapter producing it, rather than teach the generic runtime to parse arbitrary documents. Exact module boundaries and persistence-version changes require focused source inspection.

The proposed three-unit reserve is deliberately execution-scoped. The plan must define atomic consumption alongside existing autonomous and checkpoint-authorized grants and prevent replay/refill through restart or explicit replacement operations. No semantic identity detection is implied.

Native approval under delegated authority must remain distinguishable from personal human review without breaking existing artifact syntax. The plan must identify the smallest truthful provenance representation and its compatibility tests.

A few optional sandbox smoke scenarios can check prompt interactions during implementation. They are not a new benchmark platform, and omitted model runs must remain an explicit verification limitation.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user requests a bounded prototype without specification or plan files. The controller determines a small assignment in context, dispatches an implementation worker, verifies and accepts the result, and completes without creating a native package or inventing a mandatory review pair.

A user supplies a Markdown checklist with three related tasks. The controller registers work from that checklist, assigns a code-review checkpoint after the shared behavior changes, and completes only after that checkpoint passes. No XML conversion or extra specification is produced.

A controller starts one conversation-scoped task and discovers another required in-scope task. It adds the task with explicit dependencies. Existing acceptance is preserved; a review of an older scope does not automatically cover the addition.

A user delegates sensible defaults but reserves approval of the finished specification. The controller resolves intermediate decisions without an interview, presents the specification, and does not implement. In a separate fully authorized native execution, it can proceed through the delegated stages without claiming the user personally reviewed each generated file.

A user grants autonomous completion before leaving. A later task exhausts ordinary allowances. The controller diagnoses the failure and spends one recorded advance-authority unit without requesting a newer message. Replaying the grant does not refill the shared reserve, and exhaustion still prevents unbounded repetition.

A review was assigned and returns FAIL. Neither source switching nor advance authority makes that result PASS. The controller organizes bounded corrections; required review remains applicable to the resulting scope.

A user delegates implementation but reserves publication. The controller completes permitted work without publishing. An instruction to discuss an idea without files similarly remains a discussion request rather than implementation permission.

A selected native package fails its own validation. The controller reports or repairs that source within authority rather than silently reopening the same work as generic execution to evade the failure.

RepositoryEvidence.Evidence: src/plugins/workflow/tooling.ts supports standalone delegated work items with optional planRunId/planTaskId, but work_checkpoint registration requires planPath and an approved native loader.
src/plugins/workflow/checkpoints.ts defines DelegatedPlanRun with required planPath, specPath, planSha256, and specSha256, and imports definition types from the native spec linter.
src/plugins/workflow/checkpoint-io.ts validates native XML structure and approved spec/plan lifecycle. This remains useful on the native path and is not a generic plan interpreter.

src/plugins/workflow/delegated.ts validates post-stop recovery authorization with a creation timestamp at or after the relevant stop. Advance authority requires a separate bounded contract rather than removing that check.

templates/agents/vv-controller.md still contains a general large_feature_gate. templates/skills/vv-spec/SKILL.md advertises use before any implementation/planning and mandates exhaustive interview progression; vv-plan and vv-execute contain manual stage transitions that need authority-aware scoping.
src/plugins/spec-guard/index.ts already limits native artifact guarding to active .vvoc/specs paths. Preserve this boundary rather than broaden the guard to unrelated documents.
